principle.name: OVERHEAD TRAVEL IS A CHAIN OF EARNED SUPPORT DEBTS, NOT A POSE SWAP
principle.summary: Ground drive must earn the first hand latch; each overhead catch absorbs a moving pendulum before the old grip releases; the exit foot probes, earns load, then pays residual travel through a displaced recovery step.

history.highest_value_visible_defect: Overhead middle read as repeated vertical X/mannequin silhouettes; pendulum load and leg counter-shear were not legible enough.
history.correction: Exaggerate lateral pelvis/chest offset from each trusted hand, separate lead/trail legs into a broad scissor, and push exit descent into a longer diagonal while preserving support events.

history.basis: All 55 final rendered frames inspected. Readable sequence: asymmetrical ground coil -> earned mixed-support latch -> one-hand pendulum drop/bottom/upswing -> catch absorption with leg overshoot -> second single-hand traverse -> second catch -> metered descent/probe/acquire -> hand-release overshoot -> displaced recovery step -> continuing exit debt. No connector invents a support/contact event; spacing is deliberately nonuniform and support ownership is visually legible.

The final render has specific authored attitude rather than generic hanging: a toe-driven diagonal entry, crooked one-hand C arcs, wide leg counter-shear, asymmetric catch absorption, compressed high-hand/ground-foot handoff, late-arm overshoot and an exit that keeps locomotion debt. The silhouette progression is memorable, force and support causality agree, and the economy reads deliberate rather than placeholder.
